text:
Nina Ramos: Quick sync 1: spotted increased toxic outputs from Iris-9B (ptq-int4) on our multilingual holdout. Mainly Spanish and code-mixed es/en prompts. Float32 baseline not showing this.
Ethan Brooks: Oof, can you share numbers?
Nina Ramos: Ran 1k samples from the Spanish toxicity harness: float32 toxic rate 1.2%, ptq-int4 toxic rate 3.8%. English-only set unchanged ~1.1% both.
Priya Singh: Any pattern on tokenization or rare-word handling? PTQ can shift logits around subword boundaries.
Nina Ramos: Yes1: many failures around accented tokens and multiword contractions (e.g., "haz\u00eda" -> tokenized differently). We see the model pick an aggressive phrasing after a certain accent token.
Luca Marino: Can you paste the quant config + runtime?
Nina Ramos: Sure:

```
model: iris-9b-2026-03-20
quant: int4 symmetric, per-tensor, scale-calib=kl-div, clip=0.997
runtime: inferd-2.2.0 (cuda12.2), triton kernels fp16 conv
```

Nina Ramos: Also ran embedding-based toxicity classifier on outputs - embedding drift made classifier miss ~40% of toxic outputs (false negatives). Embedding cosine between float32-output and int4-output moved from ~0.98 to 0.91 on failed cases.
Ethan Brooks: That explains why eval harness missed some. Is this localized to PTQ or also seen in AQ/LLM-sim quant?
Nina Ramos: I ran a quick int6 PTQ and a mixed-precision (FP16 activations) run: int6 tox rate 1.6%, mixed-precision 1.3%. So degradation seems strongest at int4 step.
Priya Singh: Could be quant noise amplifying rare-token logits. Two mitigation paths: (A) adjust quant calibration (KL vs MSE, clip), (B) post-filter with a language-aware toxicity classifier (run on FP32 embeddings).
Luca Marino: Infra: can we repro deterministically and capture logits + tokenization diffs?
infra-bot: Provisioned replay instance: iris-replay-ptq-1733102468. Replay command: `./replay --artifact s3://redwood/iris/repro/1733102468.tar.gz --deterministic --capture-logits`

Nina Ramos: Uploaded repro + samples: https://redwood-internal/s3/iris/repro/1733102468.tar.gz (internal). Contains prompt set, outputs, embeddings, and token-level traces.
Priya Singh: Action items I propose: 1) Run calibration sweep: clip {0.99,0.995,0.999}, calib method {kl,mse} and report toxic delta. 2) Recompute embeddings on float32 for classifier, keep post-filter running for es/en mixed. 3) Add targeted Spanish red-team set with diacritics and code-mix.
Ethan Brooks: Also add a quick rollback knob in Dedicated/Optimize recommendations: recommend int6 for Spanish-heavy workloads until we fix.
Luca Marino: I'll run the deterministic replay now and attach token-diff heatmaps. ETA 1h.
Nina Ramos: Safety note: triaging as medium (behavioral reproducible, market-specific). Filing incident.
safety-bot: New incident created: SAFETY-2026-0459 1: Iris-9B int4 multilingual toxicity drift. Assigned: Priya Singh. Priority: P2. https://redwood-internal/incidents/SAFETY-2026-0459
Priya Singh: I'll put a short-term rule in the eval harness: if embedding cosine to float32 < 0.94 AND toxicity classifier score > threshold then flag for human review. Will monitor for false positives.
Nina Ramos: Thanks all 1: I'll kick off the overnight calibration sweep and post results here tomorrow. :eyes:
Ethan Brooks: Good triage. If we confirm calibration fixes, add recommendation to Optimize for model-region profiles.
Luca Marino: Dropping initial logs in ticket once replay finishes.
Nina Ramos: looping @security for visibility.
Priya Singh: Will follow up with a short doc summarizing root causes and recommended quant configs for multilingual safety.
